packageRules.description: Pi always takes its latest release; the extension is verified against the Pi it runs on, so it skips the release-age gate.

Pi updates raise the devDependency floors instead of only the lockfile. Scoped to devDependencies because bump would also rewrite the peer floors to each new Pi release, and those floors are the oldest Pi we support, raised deliberately.

Pinned to the version pi ships. Pi's extension loader aliases typebox to its own bundled copy, so our declaration only types what pi executes and must match it. It moves when pi moves, not on Renovate's schedule; the typebox pin test reports when that happens.

@types/node describes the oldest Node the code must run on rather than the newest DefinitelyTyped release or the Node mise runs, so tsc rejects APIs that are not there. It follows the engines floor's major, but no lower than 22: vitest 5 declares @types/node ^22 || >=24 as a peer, and npm cannot resolve the lockfile below that.
Renovate supports only Node 24 (its engines say ^24.11), so the toolset its own tasks run in stays there while the repo moves on.
